source_text: siquidem a primordio rerum conditor harum cum ipsis pariter compertus est, ipsis ad hoc prolatis, ut deus cognosceretur. I nec enim si aliquanto posterior Moyses primus uidetur in templo litterarum suarum deum mundi dedicasse, idcirco a Pentateucho natales agnitionis supputabuntur, cum totus Moysei stilus notitiam creatoris non instituat, sed a primordio enarret, a paradiso et Adam, non ab Aegypto et Moyse recensendam, denique maior popularitas generis humani, ne nominis quidem Moysei compotes, nedum instrumenti, deum Moysei tamen norunt; etiam tantam idolatria dominationem obumbrante, seorsum tamen illum quasi proprio nomine deum') perhibent et \'deum deorum\' et \'si deus dederit\' et \'quod deo placet\' et \'deo commendo.\' uide, an nouerint quem omnia posse testantur. nec hoc ullis Moysei libris debent. ante anima quam prophetia. animae enim a primordio conscientia dei dos est; eadem nec alia et in Aegyptiis et in Syris et in Ponticis. [Iudaeorum enim deum dicunt animae deum.] noli, barbare haeretice, priorem Abraham constituere quam mundum. et si unius familiae deus fuisset creator, tamen posterior tuo non erat, etiam Ponticis ante eum notus. accipiat igitur ab antecessore formam, a certo incertus, a cognito incognitus: numquam deus latebit, numquam deus deerit, semper intellegetur, semper audietur, etiam uidebitur, quomodo uolet. habet deus testimonia: totum hoc quod sumus et in quo sumus. sic probatur et deus et unus, dum non ignoratur, alio adhuc probari laborante.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed from the beginning of things the founder of these things is found together with them, these things having been brought forth so that God might be known. And not even if Moses, who seems to be somewhat later, is the first in the temple of his writings to have dedicated the God of the world, for this reason the birthdays of recognition will be calculated from the Pentateuch, since the whole style of Moses does not establish knowledge of the creator, but narrates from the beginning, from paradise and Adam, not from Egypt and Moses to be reckoned, finally the greater popularity of the human race, not even having possession of the name of Moses, nonetheless know the God of Moses; and even with such great domination of idolatry overshadowing, they nonetheless proclaim him separately as if with his own name God, and 'God of gods' and 'if God gives' and 'what pleases God' and 'I commend to God.' See, whether they know the one who they testify is able to do all things. Nor do they owe this to any books of Moses. Before prophecy, the soul; for the soul has been given knowledge of God from the beginning; the same, and no other, is found in the Egyptians and in the Syrians and in the Pontics. For they call the God of the soul the God of the Jews. Do not, barbarous heretic, constitute Abraham as prior to the world. And if the creator had been the God of one family, nonetheless he was not later than you, even known to the Pontics before him. Therefore, let him receive form from the predecessor, from the certain the uncertain, from the known the unknown: never will God be hidden, never will God be lacking, always he will be understood, always he will be heard, and even seen, as he wishes. God has testimonies: the whole of this which we are and in which we are. Thus God is proven and one, while not being ignored, with another still laboring to prove.
pass_b_english: From the very beginning, the Founder of all things has been known alongside creation itself, because creation was brought forth precisely so that God might be recognized. Even if Moses appears somewhat later as the first to dedicate the God of the world in the temple of his writings, that does not mean the birthday of divine recognition should be dated from the Pentateuch. Moses' entire work does not institute knowledge of the Creator; it narrates it from the beginning — from Paradise and Adam, not from Egypt and Moses. The vast majority of the human race, who never even heard the name of Moses, let alone read his books, still know the God of Moses. Even under the overwhelming domination of idolatry, they speak of him apart from their idols, as if by his own proper name: 'God of gods,' 'If God gives,' 'What pleases God,' 'I commend to God.' Look at that — they acknowledge the One they testify can do all things, and they owe none of this to any book of Moses.

Before prophecy came the soul. The soul has possessed consciousness of God from the beginning as a gift, and that same consciousness — no other — is found among Egyptians, Syrians, and Pontics alike. (They call the God of the soul the God of the Jews.) Do not, you barbarous heretic, set Abraham before the world. Even if the Creator had been the God of a single family, he would still not be later than your god; the Pontics knew him before Abraham. So let your god receive his form from the predecessor — the uncertain from the certain, the unknown from the known. God will never be hidden, never be absent; he will always be understood, always be heard, and even be seen, whenever he wishes. God has his testimonies: the whole of what we are and the world in which we live. Thus God is proven to be one, while he is not ignored — even as another still labors to prove otherwise.
